ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.40 (voucher, NS-7) to the rider for the 1.70 km of unauthorised off-route driving in segment F4; fare otherwise stands.
ruling.reasoning:
Two off-route segments are recorded: 18:17–18:23 adding 2.98 km [F3] and 18:26–18:31 adding 1.70 km [F4]; each is a deviation under RD-1 with no percentage or km threshold, and the service is RydeTAXI (metered), so extra kilometres feed the fare [F5][RD-1][RD-2]. No traffic incident qualifies: the trace marks RD-4(a) as failed for both segments, and the speed-band records on Central Expressway (band 4) and Ayer Rajah Expressway (band 5) are only corroborative and cannot exempt on their own [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Segment F3 (18:17–18:23): before it started, at 18:12, the driver asked "can I go round via Lower Delta Road?" and at 18:13 the rider replied "Sure, no problem." [F9][F10]. This is a rider message sent before 18:17:00 agreeing to a specifically named road — the rider's "no problem" is an agreement, not a refusal [F10][RD-5]. The problem is the second limb of RD-5: a named-road agreement covers driving on Lower Delta Road only, and the record must tie this segment to that road. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F11], but the fact table carries no road names for the driven path and nothing places the car on Lower Delta Road; the only thing connecting the agreement to the segment is time order, which G13 says is not enough. Per G13 the finding is therefore undetermined, not exempt. Because that finding changes the amount, the record does not settle this segment and a person must look at it [RD-5].

Segment F4 (18:26–18:31): no rider message before 18:26:25 agrees to this second deviation. The only rider message in the record is the 18:13 "Sure, no problem." answering a question about going round the jam via Lower Delta Road [F9][F10] — it agrees to that one route, not to a later, second turn-off well off the original corridor (up to 1416 m away) [F4]; RD-5 requires that the agreement contain this segment, and it does not. The driver's post-trip statement that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is his own account written after the fact and is not rider consent to the second segment [F12][RD-5][G11]. This segment therefore counts as an unexempted deviation [RD-1][RD-2].

Amount: the trace and fare record set the per-km rate at this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km = $27.52 ÷ 19.52 km = $1.4098/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. The only counted segment is F4 at 1.70 km: 1.70 × $1.4098 = $2.3967 ≈ $2.40 [F4][F5][RD-2]. 1.70 km lies outside the policy's exemptions and is recoverable, whereas the 2.98 km of F3 is left undetermined and excluded from the amount. RD-6 does not apply (no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days), so no account flag [F18][RD-6]. Sanctions against the driver under RD-6 are therefore not triggered by profile alone [F18][RD-6].

ruling.reasoning:
Two off-route segments are recorded: 18:17–18:23 adding 2.98 km [F3] and 18:26–18:31 adding 1.70 km [F4]. Both are deviations under RD-1, which sets no percentage or km threshold, and this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra kilometres enter the fare [F5][RD-1][RD-2]. No traffic incident qualifies: the trace marks RD-4(a) as failed for both segments, and the speed-band records on Central Expressway (band 4) and Ayer Rajah Expressway (band 5) are only corroborative, not a standalone exemption [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Segment F3: at 18:12 the driver asked "can I go round via Lower Delta Road?" and at 18:13 the rider replied "Sure, no problem." — a rider message sent before 18:17:00 agreeing to a specifically named road [F9][F10][RD-5]. The difficulty is the second limb of RD-5: a named-road agreement covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie the segment to it. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F11], but the fact table carries no road names for the driven path and nothing places the car on Lower Delta Road or elsewhere; only the order of events connects them, and G13 says timing alone does not suffice. The finding for F3 is therefore undetermined [RD-5][G13], and because it changes the amount, the case goes to a person.

Segment F4: no rider message before the 18:26:25 start agrees to this second deviation. The only rider agreement on record is the 18:13 reply to the question about going round via Lower Delta Road [F9][F10], which does not cover a later turn-off up to 1416 m off the corridor [F4]. The driver's post-trip statement that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is his own claim, not rider consent [F12][RD-5][G11]. This segment counts.

F3 is undetermined, so no amount can be finalised for it — if a person finds it untied to Lower Delta Road, 2.98 × $1.4098 = $4.20 is refundable [F3][F5][RD-2]. Because a decision-relevant segment is undetermined, the case must be escalated rather than executed. RD-6 does not apply: the driver has no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, so no account flag [F18][RD-6].
